- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 10–15% below true peak or adjust downward by 2–4 days.
- In high sentiment + low historical volatility, model often underestimates mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast mean.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and model shows persistent downward trend, model may underestimate support; add 0.5–2% upward bias to avoid bottoming too early.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period price rise (especially after sentiment spike); apply 1–3% upward adjustment to final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows strong upward momentum but model fails to capture it, increase forecast slope by 0.1–0.3 in early period; adjust later if sentiment flattens.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lag correction to forecast, especially if sentiment peaks early.
